title: The evening adhkar
tomorrow: she planned to read the whole Qur'an over break. it's day four. now?

cards: Dusk on a porch in Houston: the streetlights blink on one by one, a dog two houses down won't stop barking, and Dadi's lips are moving. The morning has its words, and so does the evening.
Amira sits down beside her and waits. When Dadi finishes, she tells a story instead of explaining. A man comes to the Prophet ﷺ one morning, in pain.
Last night, he says, a scorpion stung me. And the Prophet's answer isn't about the scorpion at all.

teach.h: HAD YOU SAID IT LAST NIGHT.

teach.b: In the report in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet says: had you said, when evening came, I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He created, it would not have harmed you.
That's one of the evening adhkar, the remembrances for the end of the day. They mirror the morning ones. In the morning: we have entered the morning, and the dominion belongs to God.
At dusk, in another report in Sahih Muslim: we have entered the evening, and the dominion belongs to God. Same sentence, turned toward the dark.

teach.h: SAY: HE IS ALLAH, THE ONE.
teach.b: And in Abu Dawud, the Prophet tells a companion to recite the short chapter that begins, in Pickthall's words, "Say: He is Allah, the One!" along with the two chapters of refuge after it, three times at evening and at morning, and they will be enough for him.
Notice what kind of words these are. They aren't asking for a good grade or a lucky night.
They're asking for shelter, the thing a person wants most when the light goes: a door that locks, a name to say in the dark. Dadi doesn't say them because the porch is dangerous.
She says them because the day is ending, and she'd rather end it held.

how: Muslims who keep the evening adhkar recite set remembrances from the hadith between 'Asr and Maghrib or after Maghrib, including the last three short surahs of the Qur'an three times and the line of refuge from the hadith of the scorpion.

o: a family meal blessing said at the evening table
remembrances said as the day ends, asking God for shelter
the night prayer itself, said after the sky is dark

games.q: what's said at dusk — tap the pairs.
p: refuge from the evil of what He created

s: the evening adhkar are the morning ones, turned toward the dark
we have entered the morning becomes we have entered the evening; the dominion belongs to God.
the evening words are mostly requests for success and good luck
they ask for shelter: refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He created.
in the story, the Prophet tells the man how to treat a scorpion sting
his answer is about the evening before: had you said the words of refuge, it would not have harmed you.

games.q: your little cousin is scared of the dark at bedtime and asks what she can say. her family is Muslim. what fits the evening adhkar?
o: make up a fun new rhyme together to chase the dark away.
say one of the old words of refuge with her, slowly.
tell her there's nothing to fear and switch off the light.
games.why: the evening adhkar exist for exactly this hour: words of shelter, said as the light goes. old words, said together, are the tradition's answer.

practice: Listen for one evening sound near you: a car passing, a fan, a voice in another room, your own breath. Stay with that single sound for the sit, and when your attention drifts, come back to it.
If you pray, you can say the line of refuge from Sahih Muslim once before you begin.

wordCard.voice: The evening adhkar: remembrances said as the day ends, the morning's words turned toward the dark, asking God for shelter.

orig.note: Arabic: the remembrances of the evening.

carryVoice: A line for the dusk: evening, remembered, the way Dadi ends a day. Week two, opened.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2709 (the scorpion sting; 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He created')
Sahih Muslim 2723 (we have entered the evening, and the dominion belongs to God)
Sunan Abu Dawud 5082 (al-Ikhlas and the two chapters of refuge, three times evening and morning, suffice)

sources.q: Say: He is Allah, the One!
